adult_size_in.quote: The Encyclopedia of Life states a maximum size of 2.4 in, though this number is known to vary among different sources.

notes: Article says maximum growth size has not been well studied and that the 2.4 in figure varies among sources, hence medium. No volume, temperature or temperament stated.

adult_size_in.quote: Large males may reach 15 cm in length.

aggression.quote: Electric yellows are peaceful compared to most other African cichlids.

notes: Sizes disagree inside the article: FishBase maximum 8.1 cm versus other sources 10-15 cm; took the largest stated, 15 cm = 5.9 in. Peaceful is stated only relative to other African cichlids, and the same section notes they may nip the finnage of other peaceful species and are not recommended for community aquariums.
Article is about Paracrossochilus vittatus but is a stub covering only taxonomy, range and habitat. No length, tank volume, temperature or temperament figure appears anywhere in the text.

adult_size_in.quote: The holotype has a standard length of 65.3 mm.

notes: The only length in the article is the holotype standard length, 65.3 mm = 2.6 in, which is a single type specimen rather than a stated adult maximum. Nothing else in the stub.

adult_size_in.quote: reaching up to 2 m in total length and 52.2 kg in weight

notes: Cached page is the monospecific genus Elopichthys and explicitly covers E. bambusa. 2 m = 78.7 in. The line about a fast and agile predator describes wild feeding, not aquarium temperament, so aggression left null.

adult_size_in.quote: When grown to a length of about 3.5–4 cm, the male has longer fins and a brighter color than the female.

notes: The only length given is the 3.5-4 cm size at which sexual dimorphism shows, not a stated maximum; took the top of that range, 4 cm = 1.6 in. No volume, temperature or temperament stated.

adult_size_in.quote: Wild specimens have been found up to 25 cm but those in captivity rarely grow larger than 18 cm.

notes: Took the larger stated maximum, 25 cm wild = 9.8 in; captive specimens rarely exceed 18 cm. The 26-30 C range is from the Distribution and habitat section, so it is wild water temperature rather than a stated aquarium range. Schooling and hierarchy notes are not disposition statements, so aggression left null.

adult_size_in.quote: It may attain a length of 14–16 cm

notes: Took the top of the stated range, 16 cm = 6.3 in. Article covers Botia almorhae under the common name yoyo loach. No volume, temperature or temperament stated.

Article is about Cyphotilapia gibberosa but only covers taxonomy and distribution. The only figures are collection depths (34 m, 30-40 m), which are not size, volume or temperature. Nothing extractable.

adult_size_in.quote: The largest zebra loach recorded was 9.5cm (3.74") from the tip of the snout to the base of the tail.

min_volume_gal.quote: They prefer aquariums at least 75 liters (20 gallons) in size

aggression.quote: Zebra loaches are peaceful fish suitable to tropical, freshwater community aquariums.

temp_c.quote: with a pH between 6.0 and 8.0, and temperatures from 23 - 26°C

notes: Temperature quote is from the Care Requirements section; the habitat section gives the same 23-26 C range. Article also notes they can be boisterous but rarely aggressive toward tank mates.

adult_size_in.quote: the shell of this species grows to about 2.5 cm (one inch) in diameter

temp_c.quote: This snail prefers an aquarium temperature of 22 to 26 °C.

notes: Size figure is shell diameter in an aquarium, the only length-type measurement given. Cached page is titled Vittina natalensis and matches on the common name zebra nerite.

adult_size_in.quote: The zebra oto reaches about 4.4 cm (1.7 in) in SL

notes: Article covers Otocinclus cocama under the common name zebra oto. No volume, temperature or temperament stated.

adult_size_in.quote: The zebra shark attains a length of 2.5 m, with an unsubstantiated record of 3.5 m.

notes: Used the substantiated 2.5 m = 98.4 in rather than the unsubstantiated 3.5 m record. Article says the 2019 taxonomic review makes Stegostoma tigrinum the valid name and S. fasciatum a junior synonym. Docile and not dangerous to humans describes behaviour toward divers, not tank-mate temperament, so aggression left null; the article also says the species grows far too large for the home aquarium.

adult_size_in.quote: This species reaches a length of 26.4 cm.

notes: Stub article; 26.4 cm = 10.4 in is the only figure. No volume, temperature or temperament stated.
